steps.title: Where to start: what "complement" means
steps.body: The key word is "complement". Two angles are complementary when they add up to $90^\circ$, a right angle. So the complement of an angle is whatever is missing to fill a right angle.

your_turn.prompt: As a warm-up, what is the complement of $70^\circ$?

steps.title: Set up an equation
steps.body:
Call the unknown complement $x$. Together with the given $30^\circ$ it must make a right angle. Careful: do not mix this up with the supplement, which fills $180^\circ$ instead of $90^\circ$.
$$30 + x = 90$$

your_turn.prompt: Should the complement of $30^\circ$ be acute or obtuse? Why?
your_turn.answer: Acute. It is less than $90^\circ$, since the two angles together only make $90^\circ$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Subtract $30$ from both sides: $x = 90 - 30 = 60$. Check: $30 + 60 = 90$. The answer is **$60^\circ$**.
